summary: The smart #3 is the coupe-roofed, 4.40m sister car to the smart #1, sharing that car's Geely SEA platform, 66kWh NMC pack and 200kW rear motor but stretching 130mm longer and sitting lower. Australian reviewers rate it as a quiet, well-damped semi-premium cruiser rather than the sports SUV the styling and the 3.7-second BRABUS suggest -- CarExpert's verdict is that it 'isn't a performance car' and 'is no corner carver', while praising the suspension and cabin isolation. The reservations are structural rather than dynamic: three showrooms nationally, a heavily discounted first two years on the market, and a 12.8-inch screen that swallows most vehicle functions.
pros: Costs $2,910 more than a smart #1 Pro+ for 15km more WLTP range (435km vs 420km), a 370-litre boot against the #1's 313 litres, and 130mm more length -- the practical pick of the two smart SUVs
Undercuts its SEA-platform cousin the Volvo EX30 while matching its 1,600kg braked towing rating, which is unusual for an electric SUV of this size
Premium and BRABUS add 22kW three-phase AC charging over the Pro+'s 7.4kW, cutting a 10-80 per cent AC top-up to under three hours; all three grades take 150kW DC for a sub-30-minute 10-80 per cent
Five-star ANCAP rating under the 2023 protocols (90 per cent adult, 85 per cent child occupant protection), applying to every #3 sold here since September 2024

The high-voltage battery carries a separate 8-year/150,000km warranty with a 70 per cent state-of-health guarantee, on top of the unconditional 5-year/150,000km vehicle cover -- but the battery cover requires servicing every 20,000km or 12 months at a smart-appointed dealer
cons: LSH Auto Australia runs just three showrooms -- Alexandria NSW, South Melbourne VIC and one in Brisbane -- so there is no smart sales or service point in WA, SA, Tasmania, the ACT or the NT, and clearance offers have been restricted to those three states

List prices were cut $5,000 across every grade within two years of the 2024 launch ($57,900/$61,900/$70,900 down to $52,900/$56,900/$65,900), on top of runout campaigns that put a Pro+ at $50,990 drive-away -- a saving CarExpert put at up to $11,500
Capped-price servicing runs four years/80,000km and totals $2,445 (Pro+) to $3,120 (BRABUS), which is expensive for an EV with 20,000km intervals
The coupe roofline costs rear headroom and rear visibility, and the boot is shallow with a high load lip; folding the 60/40 bench leaves a sloping floor rather than a flat one
Almost every vehicle function lives in the 12.8-inch touchscreen, and CarExpert found smart's claimed single-pedal e-Pedal mode 'fell just short' of actually stopping the car
